steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a mixing bowl, stir together the sour cream, butter, creamed corn, corn niblets, and corn muffin mix.
Pour into a casserole dish or 9-inch baking dish. Bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes or until set.

raw_recipe.headline: Three Corn Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This mixture of creamed corn, corn kernels, and corn bread mix with sour cream and butter makes a delicious side dish for meat or poultry.
raw_recipe.name: Three Corn Casserole

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a mixing bowl, stir together the sour cream, butter, creamed corn, corn niblets, and corn muffin mix.
Pour into a casserole dish or 9-inch baking dish. Bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes or until set.

review.reviewBody: Believe everyone, this is a terrific recipe! Always a big hit. Try adding an egg and a half a can of sweetened condensed milk and bake in a large iron skillet. It's awesome. We like our cornbread a little sweet. This has a great texture.

I have made this Corn Casserole recipe many times and it has been a huge hit; however, I have tweaked it to fit my taste a little better. I love the idea of a sweet Corn Casserole, so I add about half a cup sugar to the mixture before I bake it. I found it helpful to drain the kernel corn so that the casserole does not turn out "soupy". This recipe can also become a "quasi-desert" by sprinkling sugar, honey, and a small amount of butter on top during the last 10 minutes of baking. If done right this can give you a caramel-like crust.

I have made this , but with a few changes I do use the cream corn , Fresh Corn when in season. I add sauteed onions, red, green and yellow peppers and cheddar cheese or whatever cheese I have and half in half for richness , beaten egg and my own house seasoning mix and bake . My family and friends love my version of this recipe. Kimberly Gilmore

I had found a similar recipe as a crock pot dish, but I’m glad I found this one. The only thing is I can’t imagine how bland this would be w/o having added fresh zested garlic, fresh ground salt & pepper. I also topped w/ cheese. But w/ those additions it’s very delicious! I ended up baking at 400 for sometime between 25-30 minutes instead of this taking so dang long at 350.

Followed directions as listed with the following adjustments: added an egg and it was fluffier than usual. Nice. Lactose intolerant so I subbed ghee for butter and Lactaid cottage cheese blender-ed smooth for sour cream. Perfect. Baked for an hour. Bake it in a clear glass dish Until the bottom starts browning.

I love this stuff. Along with others, I add the cheese but I also add sliced jalapeños to the top of half the dish (other half plain for the kids). I melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in the dish in the oven while its preheating, allowing it to grease the pan. That creates a delicious crust. This is a great side to keep the ingredients in the pantry and cook when you're out of fresh produce.
Very easy to make and turned out delicious! Doubled the ingredients and baked in a large cast iron. I left it in the oven until it was baked thoroughly which was abt 20 mins more. PERFECT
Always a crowd pleaser! I did double it and added 2eggs. I drained the juice from one can of regular corn.
Wonderful. Per other reviewers, I added 1 egg and 1 cup of shredded cheddar, and drained the corn.

Always a hit! I do add an egg if I'm just making it as written. If I double it, I add 2 eggs and put in a 9x13 glass baking dish. Sometimes I add in a handful of cheddar cheese, sometimes without. Great either way!
I drained the can of whole kernel corn and added 1 whole egg, cooked it for one hour. It came out perfect!
My hubs loves this recipe - it’s easy and smells great when baking, like corn roasting. I add a beaten egg and a few dashes of hot sauce. It can be baked in a buttered casserole dish. So good!
Little flavor. Not enough corn. Added an egg like other recipes mentioned. Maybe a little sugar would have helped... but not worth making again.
Made it last year and it was an hit at Thanksgiving. This year I added can green chilies and hall a red bell pepper. It was yummy!

I read the comments and made some of the recommended changes. Also, I just don't like canned corn so I got fresh bi-color corn, blanched it, and cut it off the cob. This dish was DELICIOUS. Definitely on the sweet side but not too much. I used 1-1/4 sticks of unsalted butter, 1/2 box of Krusteaz Honey Cornbread mix, and 1 egg. Beat that together then added the rest of the ingredients listed (used the tube of frozen white cream style corn). Put into a casserole dish and then it took almost 1.5 hrs. @ 350 degrees to cook. You can tell it's done when it's set in the middle and light golden brown. Everyone loved it. The texture was nothing like cornbread, but dryer than corn pudding (which I liked). Because some reviews said it was bland, I added some dried Basil to half of the mixture. I loved it with and without the basil. I highly recommend this version.

I love this recipe! I always make it in an iron skillet, this way the edges get nice and crunchy! I replace the sour cream with plain Greek yogurt. I serve this corn casserole with chili on top. This is a family favorite and requested often.
This is a long time family recipe. When I go home my mom and aunt know to have this on the table. So, I am home I make for myself. I try not to eat it up in setting. It last me for 3 days it's gone.
